terminal_reason: Fixed in PR #13247 (FIX-CA-16): gpu-burst-train.yml's job `if:` now ANDs the label check with an actor-identity clause (issue.user.login == repository_owner || 'github-actions[bot]'), and scripts/ci/check_workflow_actor_guard.py is wired into run_guards.py as the permanent detector. what: HIGH (code audit CA-A13, MEASURED): gpu-burst-train.yml is triggered on `issues: opened` (reachable by any account that can open an issue on this public repo) and its job gates ONLY on `contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'gpu-burst-train')` (.github/workflows/gpu-burst-train.yml:63) -- it carries no `github.event.issue.user.login == github.repository_owner` (or equivalent) actor-identity check. Every OTHER in-scope issues-triggered workflow that reads a sensitive (non-GITHUB_TOKEN) secret DOES carry that guard (28 of 28 others, verified by regex over all 72 files in .github/workflows/ 1-74 minus the 2 excluded). gpu-burst-train.yml's job env exposes RUNPOD_API_KEY, VAST_API_KEY (Arm gate, lines 119-123) and RUNPOD_SSH_KEY (Burst step, 140-153); its 'Deliver + register bundle' step (173-217) exposes VM_SSH_KEY (SSH to the trainer VM) and its checkout uses BRANCH_PROTECTION_TOKEN (a PAT, line 257). This is exactly the 'SSH + SECRETS' profile docs/security/intrusion-surface-audit-2026-06-28.md called the worst-blast P1 category and said (section 8, item 3 / section 11) should get the identical author-guard applied to ALL remaining issues.opened-triggered privileged workflows -- gpu-burst-train.yml was created after that fast-follow (its own comments reference M19/PI-20260924) and never got it. NOT currently exploited: all recent gpu-burst-train.yml issues-event runs have triggering_actor=benbaichmankass and conclusion=skipped, and no non-owner has opened an issue on this repo since 2026-07-07 (consistent with the 'Limit interactions to collaborators' setting the June audit recorded still being active) -- but I could not read that repo setting directly via any available tool (same gap the June audit noted), so today's exposure rests on an unverified setting plus the label-permission model, with zero defense-in-depth behind it, same as every other P1 workflow before its fast-follow. No CI guard exists to catch a NEW privileged issues-triggered workflow missing this pattern (checked scripts/ci/: check_workflow_catalog.py, check_workflow_trigger_reachability.py, check_workflow_push_target.py, check_workflow_failure_swallow.py -- none checks actor-guard presence), so this is a structural gap, not a one-off. PROPOSED FIX: add the Shape-A guard from docs/security/intrusion-surface-audit-2026-06-28.md section 9 to gpu-burst-train.yml's job `if:` (AND the label check with `github.event.issue.user.login == github.repository_owner || == 'github-actions[bot]'`), and add a CI guard (check_workflow_actor_guard.py) that fails when a new/changed issues:-triggered workflow reading a secrets.* value lacks this pattern.
